english: Neighbour, your smoke is going out of the roof. Fire has caught the roof. Bring water! Take a full pot; pour it onto the roof. The fire died. Is your daughter out? She is out with her own mother. My house was spared(?). I thank you. Is your seat whole? It is whole.
uncertain: gʷḗn te gʷr̥néHmi: taken as a thanks formula

english: Neighbour, your walls stand. They stand. The roof is heavy; one man cannot lift it. Can you lift it? My sons and I will lift it. When will you come? We will come at dawn. Come, and I will cook meat for you.
uncertain: pékʷōh₂ read as 1sg subjunctive 'I will cook'

english: Master of the house, your door is not straight and the wind comes inside. I know that. My son broke the door last year. Do you complain? I complain. Shall I lean a stone against the door? Don't lean it; I will bind the door with a rope. Guest, sit by the hearth. I sit; your hearth warms (me).

What are you weaving, mother? I am weaving withies between the posts. Will you help me? I will help you. Where are the withies? They lie by the fire. Bring them to me. These withies are long. Shall I cut them? Don't cut them; long withies have held up the wall.

Sister-in-law, snow is coming and our roof is not whole. My brother will roof it early. He said that yesterday too. Shall we roof it now? Do women climb roofs? The men will laugh. Let them laugh; we shall be warm. Sister-in-law, you are bold.

How many wagons have we already filled? Seven wagons. How many draw them? Ten oxen and four cows. Now the cows draw two wagons. The cows are pregnant/heavy. They are strong. When do we leave? When the sun shines.
